facts.raw_span: A woman in her 50s presented with a 2.5-year history of severe urticaria
chronic pruritus, which was worsening and refractory to treatment
Previous medication trials of doxepin, monteleukast, hydroxizine, famotidine, fexofenadine, and ranitidine provided only minimal benefit
She initially responded well to omalizumab but became refractory after 1 week of treatment
edematous, superficial wheals and plaques on the arms, back, and thighs, along with dermatographism
dermal edema with sparse chronic inflammation and dilated blood vessels within the superficial dermis, consistent with dermal hypersensitivity
Skin-prick allergy testing was negative
Food elimination diet results were negative
Skin patch testing showed positive results for methylisothiazolinones
